Auto-summary: Quick hands-on lab exploring Redwood Console trace playback and request forensics. Focus on reproducing a customer error path, KV cache/ prefix cache behavior, fallbacks between model variants, and retention/compliance controls (audit logs, KMS). Agreed next steps: run a 24h replay of sample traces and share the cost/latency profile.
Topics covered: 1) trace playback UI and filters; 2) request-level logs and correlated spans; 3) error analysis patterns; 4) routing/fallback behavior; 5) private deployment / VPC considerations.

[00:00:05] Maya Patel: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, quick intros? this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE and i'll run the agenda, arjun is our solutions engineer and he'll do the deep console walkthrough.
[00:00:18] Dr. Lena Ortiz: hi lena here, SRE lead at HelioPharm. we run models for dosing guidance in production, so latency and correctness both matter, uh, a lot.
[00:00:25] Noah Kim: Noah, platform. curious about request logs size & retention, and how we can replay a day of traffic without burning a ton of tokens.
[00:00:30] Priya Rao: Priya, CTO. i'll listen in for compliance bits.
[00:00:33] Arjun Singh: great thanks, let's jump in. i'll share my screen and start in the Console -> Trace Playback. if anyone can't see ping maya.
[00:00:45] [screen share begins]
[00:01:05] Arjun Singh: alright so this is the trace index, we've got 14k traces in this project, i'm filtering to the last 24 hours, and i'm going to show a failed path that lena sent over - it shows a model timeout then fallback to a smaller variant and later a KV cache miss.
[00:01:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: yeah the error triggers when patients' notes hit about 4k tokens, we see a burst of timeouts around 9am PST on tuesday.
[00:01:40] Arjun Singh: okay i'm applying the token-length filter and the latency spike, you can see aggregated latency heatmap here, this is the request histogram.
[00:01:55] Maya Patel: quick note, our histogram buckets are adaptive; they change based on the distribution, so when you zoom on 4k+ tokens you get finer buckets.
[00:02:12] [00:02:12] Noah Kim: is that live or sampled? we can't pull everything for compliance reasons.
[00:02:18] Arjun Singh: good question, the index is a combination - traces are retained as metadata for the full 30 days by default, but full request payloads are sampled; you can configure deterministic sampling for specific routes so all e.g. /dose-eval requests are kept.
[00:02:35] [00:02:35] Dr. Lena Ortiz: so deterministic sampling ties to route name and model id?
[00:02:42] Arjun Singh: yep you can pin it to route+model+customer tag; that way we only store full payloads for anything matching the signature you give.
[00:02:55] [00:02:55] Maya Patel: and for SOC2/ISO, we offer an audit log export and KMS-backed encryption of request payloads - arjun will show encryption toggles in a sec.
[00:03:08] [00:03:08] Arjun Singh: jumping into a single trace now - top-level view shows timeline, spans, and any fallback events. here you can see the initial tokenization span, then inference span where the timeout occurs, followed by the fallback to a 7B variant.
[00:03:30] [00:03:30] Arjun Singh: the span annotations show exit codes, GPU utilization, and kernel warnings; sometimes transcription calls them "kernel warn" but it's basically a tensor-core oom or kernel launch stall.
[00:03:45] [00:03:45] Dr. Lena Ortiz: can you show the raw request body? we need to check prompt prefixes for pii leakage risk.
[00:03:51] Arjun Singh: sure, here's the payload inspector. note: if payload is redacted due to compliance settings you'll see a redaction banner. for this trace the payload is available - you can copy or download.
[00:04:08] [00:04:08] Noah Kim: how big are those payload blobs typically? i'm worried about egress and storage cost.
[00:04:14] Arjun Singh: we store compressed blobs, typical payloads are 2-20KB compressed; embeddings and attachments increase that. our suggestion is to enable route-level deterministic sampling only for the few routes you're actively debugging.
[00:04:30] [00:04:30] Priya Rao: what about KMS - who holds the keys if we do Private?
[00:04:36] Arjun Singh: for Private deployments you retain keys in your KMS/HSM. for Dedicated and Hosted we integrate with customer KMS via envelope encryption; we can give a diagram. maya i'll flag the network diagram for priya.
[00:04:49] Maya Patel: noted - will include network and kms integration diagram in the follow-up.
[00:04:55] [00:04:55] Arjun Singh: back to the trace timeline — here's where Redwood routed the request: primary model was rwd-large-v1, fallback policy triggered after 6s and routed to rwd-medium-q4, you can see the fallback event recorded with reason code and cost delta.
[00:05:14] [00:05:14] Dr. Lena Ortiz: that cost delta number is important, can you show the per-token breakdown for the fallback?
[00:05:21] Arjun Singh: yes, there's a token-cost panel that pops out; it shows tokens generated, tokens billed, and unit cost normalized by model. note that quantized variants like rwd-medium-q4 have lower per-token cost but sometimes higher latency for very long contexts.
[00:05:40] [00:05:40] Noah Kim: earlier you mentioned KV cache miss - can you show where that appears in the trace?
[00:05:47] Arjun Singh: sure, here — we annotate KV cache hits/misses as spans; in this trace the first chunk was a cache miss because the request used a new prompt prefix, so the runtime had to re-compute key values which cost us time.
[00:06:00] [00:06:00] Dr. Lena Ortiz: so is prefix caching automatic or do we need to configure it on the client?
[00:06:06] Arjun Singh: prefix caching is automatic for repeated prefixes, but you can also pin prefixes via the SDK to force caching server-side. there's also a TTL per-prefix setting.
[00:06:22] [00:06:22] Maya Patel: many customers see a big win from prefix pinning for conversational assistants that have a stable system prompt.
[00:06:30] [00:06:30] Noah Kim: can you simulate a cache warm-up on the Console? like run synthetic warm calls?
[00:06:36] Arjun Singh: yes in the Console there's a 'Warm' action on the route which will push a synthetic set of requests to warm KV caches across the pool; we usually suggest a small burst during deploy windows.
[00:06:48] [00:06:48] Dr. Lena Ortiz: if we warm, does that increase our billed tokens?
[00:06:52] Arjun Singh: warm calls are billed same as normal, but you can mark them as internal so they don't count against end-user quotas; cost still incurred.
[00:07:06] [00:07:06] Priya Rao: let's talk about replicating the incident - can we replay the exact sequence for the 9am spike?
[00:07:13] Arjun Singh: yes we can. Arjun continuing: in the playback mode you can select a time window and choose 'replay in staging' which will re-execute the requests against a pinned model in a sandbox. i'll demo: selecting 08:45-09:15, selecting the route, and clicking replay.
[00:07:32] [00:07:32] [clicks]
[00:07:40] [00:07:40] Arjun Singh: ok replay job created - note that replays are rate-limited and you can throttle to match production QPS; we also provide a dry-run where we only simulate without consuming quota if you don't need full inference.
[00:07:55] [00:07:55] Dr. Lena Ortiz: dry-run could be useful for initial triage, yes. but for root cause we'll probably want the full replay.
[00:08:03] [00:08:03] Noah Kim: what about routing policies - is it possible a node was overloaded and triggered fallbacks? how is that surfaced?
[00:08:10] Arjun Singh: routing telemetry includes per-node CPU/GPU saturation metrics and a routing decision trace. if a pool reports overload the routing tier logs an overloaded flag and you'll see increased fallback rates in the route analytics.
[00:08:24] [00:08:24] Maya Patel: also our autoscaling policies can be tuned - you can configure target latency, buffer queue length, and max burst nodes. we'll share sample configs that mirror HelioPharm's QPS.
[00:08:36] [00:08:36] [00:08:36] Dr. Lena Ortiz: what about private deployment though - network egress is restricted for our infra team, we might need an on-prem option.
[00:08:44] Arjun Singh: for Private we ship a control plane and you run inference in your VPC or on-prem; logs and traces stay within your network by default. we've done air-gapped installs for pharma customers; it requires a connector for updates and a staging sync process.
[00:09:03] [00:09:03] Priya Rao: compliance will want signed audit trails for who accessed traces. can we get a per-user audit export?
[00:09:10] Arjun Singh: yes the audit logs include user, action, timestamp, and resources accessed. you can export as JSON or append to your SIEM. for hosted setups we stream audit logs to customer S3 or BigQuery.
[00:09:24] [00:09:24] Maya Patel: i'm going to drop the SOC2 artifact link in chat now - it covers audit log retention and encryption flow.
[00:09:30] [chat link posted]
[00:09:36] [00:09:36] Arjun Singh: jumping into error analysis - here's a common pattern: long context -> tokenization spike -> kv miss -> model OOM -> fallback. the console flags this as an "inference chain" and suggests remediation steps like prefix pinning, chunking, or model aliasing.
[00:09:56] [00:09:56] Dr. Lena Ortiz: chunking might break some of our prompt semantics, have you got examples for safely chunking clinical notes?
[00:10:04] Arjun Singh: we have a chunking helper in the SDK that preserves question/answer pairs and folds metadata. it's not perfect for every use case but we've got a clinic-specific pattern pack we can share.
[00:10:16] [00:10:16] Noah Kim: Arjun, can you show the correlation between request logs and our external observability? we use Datadog.
[00:10:22] Arjun Singh: sure - there's a correlation pane where you can paste a trace id and it will link to any external link we have mapped, like Datadog or Splunk. we also include a trace id header in requests so you can join on that side.
[00:10:36] [00:10:36] [00:10:36] Priya Rao: who typically triggers a replay job - are there RBAC controls? we don't want engineers accidentally replaying production traffic.
[00:10:45] Arjun Singh: RBAC is granular - replay create requires 'ops:replay' permission which you can limit to a role. replay approvals are optional; you can enable an approval workflow that routes to a pager duty or Slack channel for sign-off.
[00:10:58] [00:10:58] Dr. Lena Ortiz: nice. can the approval include a scrub step for PII?
[00:11:04] Arjun Singh: yes we support pre-replay transformation hooks where you can run a lambda to scrub sensitive fields; if the hook fails the replay won't start.
[00:11:14] [00:11:14] Maya Patel: quick aside, a lot of customers confuse 'trace retention' with 'payload retention'. traces (metadata) are cheap and kept longer; full payloads are controlled by sampling.
[00:11:25] [00:11:25] Noah Kim: back to cost - do you have a sample cost report from a 24h replay?
[00:11:32] Arjun Singh: yes i'll pull an example. this one replays 60k requests, default throttled to 200 qps, cost was $1,200 and average latency increased about 15% due to serialization overhead in staging. i'll attach the CSV in follow-up.
[00:11:52] [00:11:52] Dr. Lena Ortiz: what about cold-starts on shards? during the spike we also saw a flurry of node restarts. can the trace show node restart correlations?
[00:12:00] Arjun Singh: node events are correlated; you'll see a node lifecycle span in the trace. if a restart overlapped the request the trace will show the restart and the routing layer will log an eviction event.
[00:12:12] [00:12:12] Priya Rao: how do you instrument that without too much noise? we don't want pages for every tiny restart.
[00:12:19] Arjun Singh: thresholds for alerting are configurable; we recommend a cluster-level SLO and to only alert on sustained error budgets or repeated evictions.
